title: if you work ai assisted, this is a game changer for Godot devs.
author: Environmental-Lie496
selftext:
so im no AI maximalist and no AI hater, and I definitely dont want to get into the politics or anything controversial. I *personally* don't believe in pure vibe coding to ship a flagship project, games are way too living and breathing projects *to me a*nd need too much hands on attention for it to hit the heart of players in my opinion (but I do not have any problem with those who dont see it that way). However, I am a firm believer in ai assisted engineering and coding as a viable amazing tool. Im not the strongest coder, but I know systems, problem solving and building architectures. Many think Godot isn't good for AI assisted dev, but that couldn't be more wrong. Find a good MCP! Using a Godot MCP, I sat and worked on drawing my pixel art animations while GPT 5.4 wired a complex Animation Tree state machine. It is clean, light, and with just a few minor adjustments, it was production ready and polished. I mean, clean. Heres the kicker : I did have to do extensive instructing and planning beforehand of how I wanted it done, how I envisioned the blending of animations, what tools/ methods and constraints  I wanted it to use. But once I pathed it out, it literally took a 1-2 day long project into a 30 min waiting session. One note, GPT 5.4 has been INFINITELY better to execute lately, but I use Opus to plan out the architecture. Claude just overthinks it and finds the sloppiest most over engineered way to do it, which is a bit surprising in this case. Sonnet has been better than Opus lately, but that's a convo for another day.  I use Pi to toggle back and forth between GPT and different Claude models in real time and it doesnt ruin context, and they can basically "collaborate", kinda not really. If your a person like me, who wants to have their hands in their entire project and own it but in my case, I  health issues, and my father recently passed and just life like everyone else - this can really give you so much more bandwidth in an already extremely daunting task of creating a game.  I dont want to recommend any specific map quite yet, im trying out a few and so far most can get it done, but some confuse the model and can make a mess. It took a while and some GOOD MD FILES and a custom skill to really make it work. I think those are a bit more important than the actual MCP you use. 

  
Best wishes to all on all of your projects!
